A skipped or stopped loop-back supplies no success; the already-started Iterator cannot be skipped and has no qualifying failed-safely exception, so no path advances it.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Iterator action repeats its child steps for each item in a list. A finite Iterator placed directly after a manual trigger stops advancing when a loop Filter rejects an item, leaving its completed continuation unstarted and the saved execution Running.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Form workflow action collects user answers before the automation continues. Entering a valid answer in one Number field re-enables workflow Form submission while another field still displays invalid text and its validation error.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Form filler uses one shared error value for all fields. A valid Number field calls the shared error callback with undefined, overwriting another field’s error and enabling Submit. Invalid text remains local to its input and does not update the stored answer, so submission omits it or sends the previous valid number.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Form workflow action collects user answers before the automation continues. Enter an invalid answer in one Number field of a running Form, then a valid answer in another. Submit becomes enabled even though the first field still has invalid text and an error.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s HTTP Request action sends a configured request, including a URL, headers and optional body. In an HTTP Request action, add a content-type property to a Key/Value request body. The editor treats the body property as a restricted HTTP header and removes it from the saved body, even though it is ordinary payload data in this context.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared KeyValuePairInput applies the reserved-header content-type guard to every caller and filters flagged rows from onChange. BodyInput reuses that component without a header-only switch, so valid payload properties are filtered before the debounced body save.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s HTTP Request action sends a configured request, including a URL, headers and optional body. A newly entered content-type property in an HTTP Request Key/Value body is incorrectly treated as a reserved header and omitted from saved body configuration.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s HTTP Request action sends a configured request, including a URL, headers and optional body. Enter a Content-Type HTTP header that normal editing rejects, then delete a different header. That removal saves the previously rejected Content-Type row; after reload it is treated as automatically managed, so it cannot be edited or deleted.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The edit reducer filters non-managed reserved keys, but the remove reducer serializes every remaining nonempty row without that validation. Reload classifies the saved reserved key as automatically managed, suppresses its warning and disables editing and deletion.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s HTTP Request action sends a configured request, including a URL, headers and optional body. Deleting an unrelated header saves a manually entered Content-Type header that normal editing rejects, then reload turns it into a disabled managed row.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty workflows are automations made of a starting trigger and connected action steps. Reconnect an existing arrow between workflow steps. The reconnection saves correctly, but the editor also starts adding a new step, opens Select Action and places a temporary Add an Action card over the destination. This is an extra creation interaction after reconnection, not failure to save the new arrow.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The reconnect drag records connection-start information used by drag-to-create. The ordinary connect handler clears it, while the reconnect path does not. The shared connect-end handler can therefore start node creation after reconnecting. Exact callback ordering is inferred from the source and observed controls.
reproductionPaths: Twenty workflows are automations made of a starting trigger and connected action steps. Reconnect an existing workflow arrow to another step. The connection saves, but Select Action also opens and a temporary Add an Action step covers the destination.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s schedule trigger starts an automation at configured recurring times. Typing a valid two-digit schedule hour can restore a stale prefix; editing only minutes then saves the wrong hour.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Hour changes dispatch saves per keystroke. A completed response updates the flow using its captured submitted trigger, and the controlled input synchronizes to that echoed value. An older response can restore a stale prefix; the minute handler copies that stale hour into its next save. Exact server commit ordering is not independently traced.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s schedule trigger starts an automation at configured recurring times. Type a valid two-digit hour into a schedule and then change only its minutes. The hour can revert to an earlier single-digit prefix and that wrong hour is saved along with the new minutes.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Delay action pauses an automation for a duration or until a specified date and time. Type a Delay duration and press Tab to leave the numeric input. Focus stays in the input instead of moving away, so the edit never reaches its save-on-leave step and reload restores the old duration.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Delay stores duration edits locally and calls its action update only on blur. The number input uses TextInput hotkeys with no Tab callback. The default handler prevents the native Tab action, so focus stays in the input, blur never occurs and no duration update is submitted.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Delay action pauses an automation for a duration or until a specified date and time. Typing a Delay duration and pressing Tab leaves focus in the same input, so its save when leaving the field never executions and reload restores the old duration.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saves automation configurations in versions; a draft is editable and an Active version is published. After Use as Draft creates a new saved draft, reopening workflow versions history can omit it while the versions count includes it.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The history entry reuses cached list state after draft creation. The new draft exists and can be opened, while the reopened history list can retain its old two rows. Exact cache timing is inferred.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saves automation configurations in versions; a draft is editable and an Active version is published. Create a new draft with Use as Draft, then reopen workflow version history. The saved draft can be missing from the history rows while the version count includes it.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Iterator action repeats its child steps for each item in a list. Backspace temporarily removes an Iterator loop-start connection, then the connection returns and remains after reload.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The keyboard edge callback omits sourceConnectionOptions. Without the Iterator loop option, the server checks ordinary nextStepIds and returns unchanged; the observed response has empty triggerDiff and stepsDiff. The trash callback supplies the loop option.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Iterator action repeats its child steps for each item in a list. Select an Iterator’s loop-start arrow and press Backspace. The arrow briefly disappears, then returns and remains after reload; deleting it through its on-screen trash action works.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty workflows are automations made of a starting trigger and connected action steps. Right-clicking the canvas, choosing Add node, then selecting Delay leaves Select Action instead of creating the node. A second selection works; plus/header insertion controls work.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Canvas Add Node opens the step-creation side panel through a shared node-creation state transition; the first action choice can race with creation-panel state initialization and is consumed without creating the intended step. Exact ordering is inferred from the creation-state path and the verified first-choice/second-choice control.
reproductionPaths: Twenty workflows are automations made of a starting trigger and connected action steps. Right-click the workflow diagram, choose Add node and select Delay. The first choice leaves the action picker open instead of creating the step, while a second selection works; other add-step controls work.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s If/Else workflow step chooses between alternative paths based on conditions. After Delay is changed to If/Else, reloaded, and changed back to Delay, two generated EMPTY branch placeholders remain disconnected and survive reload. Direct If/Else deletion removes its placeholders.
logicalBugs.rootCause: If/Else creation persists branch endpoints as separate steps. Type replacement rebuilds only the controller while retaining other saved steps and losing its branch links. Diagram generation renders the retained endpoints. The explicit delete path cleans up empty branch children; analogous cleanup on replacement is inferred rather than an explicit maintainer promise.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s If/Else workflow step chooses between alternative paths based on conditions. Change a Delay action to If/Else, reload and change it back to Delay. Two empty branch-placeholder steps remain disconnected and persist after reload; directly deleting an If/Else removes its empty placeholders.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty records each execution of an automation as a workflow run, with a Flow diagram and step details. Completed and stopped workflow executions show their start and end timestamps but no overall Duration in the record details. The requested elapsed-time value is absent at the execution level; this does not claim that individual step timings are missing.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The inspected run model and page layout contain timestamps but no run-level duration display/calculation. Per-step durationMs observability is a separate feature.
reproductionPaths: Twenty records each execution of an automation as a workflow run, with a Flow diagram and step details. Inspect a completed or stopped workflow execution. Its details show start and end timestamps but no execution-level Duration, unlike the requested elapsed-time display.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can fill workflow inputs with entered values or references to a trigger or earlier step. Phone fields in workflow Create Record convert national-number text to a number and strip significant leading zeroes. The altered digits persist after reopening and are used in the created Person, including Italian +39 numbers.
logicalBugs.rootCause: FormPhoneFieldInput routes the phone national-number text through FormNumberFieldInput/castAsNumberOrNull. Numeric coercion removes significant leading zero characters before constructing the saved phone value.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can fill workflow inputs with entered values or references to a trigger or earlier step. In a People Create Record action, choose a country and enter a national phone number with a significant leading zero. The zero is removed, the altered digits survive reload, and the created Person receives the altered phone number.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s If/Else workflow step chooses between alternative paths based on conditions. Duplicating an individual If/Else workflow action leaves its copy sharing the original branch Filter nodes. Even the original matching route can remain Not started while the execution reports Completed; removing the duplicate restores execution.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Individual action duplication clones the If/Else controller and its branch/filter references without allocating independent companion branch IDs. The original and copy therefore share branch execution dependencies, preventing the original matching route from running independently.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s If/Else workflow step chooses between alternative paths based on conditions. Duplicate an individual If/Else step, leaving the copy disconnected. The copy still shares the original child Filter steps, so the original matching route can remain Not started while execution reports Completed; deleting the copy restores that route.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Delay action pauses an automation for a duration or until a specified date and time. A workflow Delay whose scheduled date is mapped from malformed text fails with an internal serialization error instead of an invalid-date diagnostic. Valid future dates complete, while missing and past dates receive input-specific errors.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Delay scheduled-date edit forwards a malformed date into its workflow update/GraphQL serialization path; validation does not classify it as an input error before the DateTime serialization failure is surfaced.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Delay action pauses an automation for a duration or until a specified date and time. Feed malformed text from a Form into a Delay’s scheduled date. Execution fails with an internal serialization error rather than an invalid-date diagnostic; valid future dates complete and missing or past dates receive input-specific errors.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Form workflow action collects user answers before the automation continues. Long Form-field labels overflow the workflow input-settings row at narrow widths, clipping the settings close button and adjacent controls such as Placeholder. The top-level panel close remains usable.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Form field settings use a horizontal layout with unbounded label content and fixed adjacent controls; long labels grow their intrinsic width rather than ellipsizing/shrinking, clipping type/delete/settings controls in narrow panels.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Form workflow action collects user answers before the automation continues. Give a Text Form input a long label and open its settings at phone width. The row overflows to the right, hiding the input-settings close button and clipping Placeholder; the top-level panel close remains visible.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saves automation configurations in versions; a draft is editable and an Active version is published. A discarded Workflow Version retains generic Restore controls on its deleted detail page, but both the banner and header Restore are rejected as unauthorized and leave the version deleted.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Discarded versions use generic deleted-record detail chrome, which offers Restore, but workflow-version restore pre-query hooks unconditionally reject the generic restore operation. The specialized discard lifecycle does not expose a corresponding supported Restore action.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saves automation configurations in versions; a draft is editable and an Active version is published. Discard a saved workflow draft, then reopen that version’s retained page. Its deleted banner and header offer Restore, but both are rejected and the version stays deleted after reload.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Iterator action repeats its child steps for each item in a list. After the sole action inside an Iterator loop is deleted, inserting its replacement through the empty loop edge places it over the Iterator controller. The overlap persists in reopened and completed-execution diagrams although the replacement remains configurable and executes.
logicalBugs.rootCause: After the sole Iterator loop-body action is deleted, edge insertion into the empty loop uses generic edge/node placement without reserving the controller loop geometry, so the replacement action position overlaps the Iterator controller.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Iterator action repeats its child steps for each item in a list. Delete the only action inside an Iterator loop and insert a replacement through its empty loop arrow. The new step overlaps the Iterator controller in the saved and execution diagrams, although it remains editable and can execute.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can fill workflow inputs with entered values or references to a trigger or earlier step. An invalid numeric replacement remains visible in Create Record while Test executes the earlier saved value, making the displayed draft misleading.
logicalBugs.rootCause: FormNumberFieldInput retains invalid locally typed text while rejecting it through its error callback. Workflow Test executes the last successfully saved mapping, but the editor does not make that saved/local divergence clear when the rejected text remains displayed.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can fill workflow inputs with entered values or references to a trigger or earlier step. An invalid numeric replacement remains visible in Create Record while Test executes the earlier saved value, making the displayed draft misleading.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s schedule trigger starts an automation at configured recurring times. A displayed valid five-field custom cron expression (text specifying a recurring schedule) can coexist with an invalid-expression description and duplicate upcoming execution times.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CronExpressionHelper computes its description and upcoming occurrences through preview parsing of the entered expression/timezone. The standard five-minute expression is accepted by the scheduler but the preview path can misclassify its description and duplicate occurrences; exact parser divergence is not established by the retained source evidence. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s schedule trigger starts an automation at configured recurring times. A displayed valid five-field custom cron expression (text specifying a recurring schedule) can coexist with an invalid-expression description and duplicate upcoming execution times.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can fill workflow inputs with entered values or references to a trigger or earlier step. A preloaded Create Person action already contains a Company reference in an older saved format. The editor shows an empty selection even though a retained execution resolves that reference and links the Person correctly. Newly authored Company references display normally; this is misrepresentation of the existing mapping, not demonstrated failure to create the link.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Create Record formats the stored relation mapping through the current objectRecord relation-field shape before rendering FormSingleRecordPicker. A legacy companyId-style mapping can execute successfully yet fail that current-shape lookup and display an empty selection.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can fill workflow inputs with entered values or references to a trigger or earlier step. Open the preloaded Create Person action that already contains an older-style Company reference. The editor shows an empty Select placeholder although historical execution resolves that reference and links the Person correctly; newly created mappings (saved input values or references) display normally.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Delay action pauses an automation for a duration or until a specified date and time. Rapidly updating two numeric duration fields in a Delay action causes the second input to revert to its previously saved value. Waiting between edits allows each value to save.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Each Delay duration blur submits a full duration object captured from local state. An earlier update response synchronizes action/localDuration while a second field edit is pending, so the later commit can spread an older sibling value over the newer edit.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Delay action pauses an automation for a duration or until a specified date and time. Rapidly updating two numeric duration fields in a Delay action causes the second input to revert to its previously saved value. Waiting between edits allows each value to save.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty workflows are automations made of a starting trigger and connected action steps. Duplicating a workflow through the user interface attributes the new workflow to System instead of the initiating member. Normal workflow creation records the member correctly.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The workflow duplication service constructs new workflow/version records without passing the initiating actor through the createdBy field; the standard actor-field fallback is System, unlike ordinary user-authored workflow creation.
reproductionPaths: Twenty workflows are automations made of a starting trigger and connected action steps. Duplicate a workflow through the user interface. Its Created by field is System instead of the initiating member, while ordinary workflow creation records that member correctly.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty workflows are automations made of a starting trigger and connected action steps. After deleting, restoring, and reactivating an active Record-created workflow, a single matching record creation launches two executions and duplicates action output.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Parent restoration undeletes automated trigger records as well as versions. Reactivation registers/enables a trigger without reconciling that restored registration, so the database-event listener can match two registrations for the same workflow/event and launch duplicate runs.
reproductionPaths: Twenty workflows are automations made of a starting trigger and connected action steps. After deleting, restoring, and reactivating an active Record-created workflow, a single matching record creation launches two executions and duplicates action output.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Delay action pauses an automation for a duration or until a specified date and time. Deleting a workflow during a pending Delay and restoring it after the deadline can strand the original execution at Running/Pending with later actions unstarted. A new execution of the restored same-version workflow completes normally.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Workflow restore undeletes run/version records but does not recreate the expired/consumed delayed resume job. resume-delayed-workflow can ignore or terminate work while its run is deleted, leaving the later restored run RUNNING/PENDING after the scheduled resume time.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Delay action pauses an automation for a duration or until a specified date and time. Delete a workflow during a pending Delay and restore it after that Delay’s deadline. The original execution remains Running/Pending with its next step unstarted during the observed checks, while a new execution of the restored same-version workflow completes normally.
